sections.h2: Offices that handle your Hernando County tax bill
sections.html:
Three elected offices split the work. The property appraiser values parcels and grants exemptions. The tax collector mails the bills and takes the money. The clerk files deeds and runs tax deed auctions. A seller will probably deal with all three before closing.

The tax collector is at 20 N. Main Street, Room 112, Brooksville, FL 34601, and takes questions at tc@hernandocounty.us. Homestead exemptions, assessed values and name or address changes for notices belong to the appraiser. The Hernando County Property Appraiser has offices in Brooksville and Spring Hill, plus a tax estimator and a parcel search on its site.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, parcel search, ownership changes on the roll.
  • Tax Collector: tax bills, payments, installment plan, certificate sale.
  • Clerk: recorded deeds and tax deed sales.

sections.h2: When is Hernando County property tax due?
sections.html:
Bills go out in November. Payment is accepted through March 31, and any account still open on April 1 is delinquent.

A November payment saves 4 percent. The discount shrinks by a point each month until February, and March carries none. For current-year payments sent during a discount month, the postmark counts. E-check payments online are free for current and delinquent bills. Cards carry a $2.75 minimum or 2.5% processing fee, which goes to a third-party vendor.

Tangible personal property tax covers furniture, fixtures and equipment in businesses and rental properties. It arrives on the same bill and earns the same discounts. Owners who file a return by April 1 can claim a $25,000 exemption, so a landlord selling a rental should ask whether an account like that exists for the address.

sections.h2: How does the Hernando County installment plan work?
sections.html:
The plan splits the bill into four quarterly payments, and each installment can only be paid in its own month. Enrollment opens every November 1 and closes April 30. It is confirmed once the first June payment goes through.

Hernando County Tax Collector installment schedule
Due dateDiscount
June 306%
July 31None, keeps you on the plan
September 304.5%
December 313%
March 31Final payment, no discount

A late installment must be paid together with the next one. A balance still unpaid on April 1 is delinquent and no discount applies. Dropping out of the plan means giving up the discounts. The statute behind it is section 197.222.

Outside the plan, partial payments on the current year are possible from November 1 through March 31. You sign an application, forfeit every discount, and may make only five partial payments, with the balance due by March 31.

A Hernando County homestead exemption takes up to $50,000 off the taxable value of the home you live in. You must own it and make it your permanent Florida residence by January 1 of the year you apply.

Applications now being taken cover tax year 2027 and are due March 1, 2027. Anything filed after that counts toward 2028. You can apply at an appraiser office, by mail or on the secure online portal. Statewide, the Save Our Homes cap holds yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is smaller, and the Florida Revenue chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.

On the bill, the tax collector rolls every exemption into a single dollar figure under the word Exemption. When a home sells, the appraiser drops the seller's exemption and cap starting the next year. The buyer has to file a new application to start fresh.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the certificate sale
sections.html:
Delinquent Hernando County tax earns 3% interest from April 1, gets listed in a local newspaper, and picks up advertising and collection fees. The tax collector auctions tax certificates online through LienHub at the end of May. May 29 is the last day to pay before the sale.

  • Bidding starts at 18 percent interest and falls in steps toward 0.25 percent.
  • The winning bidder pays the taxes and holds a first lien on the parcel.
  • A homestead parcel with a taxable amount under $250.00, or one in litigation, is struck off to the county.
  • A certificate lives seven years unless bankruptcy interrupts it.
  • After two years the holder may ask for a tax deed sale, which the clerk conducts.

Delinquent bills can be paid by any method, but a parcel in tax deed status needs certified funds. If nobody bids at a deed sale, the land goes on a list of lands available for taxes, and the county gets the first 90 days to buy it.

sections.h2: Closing on a Hernando County sale
sections.html:
The seller pays off the tax from closing funds, and the recorded deed is what moves the bill to the buyer. Once the clerk has a finished deed, the appraiser changes the owner on the roll. The tax collector's record follows after the next certified tax roll in October.

Florida's documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents for each $100 of the price in every county but Miami-Dade, and each party to the deed is liable. The closing statement should split the current year's bill between buyer and seller. If the property has a tangible personal property account on the same bill, mention it to the title company.

Millage rates are set by each taxing authority. The tax collector names the county commission, the City of Brooksville, the school board and the regional water district as examples. The appraiser posts a millage report after final roll certification. For the rate on your parcel, read the TRIM notice mailed in August or ask the tax collector.

A few plain steps make this smoother. Ask the title company to request a written payoff from the tax collector close to the closing date, since balances can change. Have your parcel number and a copy of your deed handy when you call an office. Check every tax year for a balance, not just the current one. If back taxes or a certificate would slow a buyer who relies on a mortgage, a cash buyer who skips lender appraisal and underwriting lets the title company clear the debt from your proceeds at the table.

Petitions go to the Value Adjustment Board, filed at the clerk's office on one of the DR-486 forms. They are due within 25 days of the August TRIM mailing from the appraiser. A petition filed after the deadline on the notice is out of time, so write down the date the envelope arrives.

A refused homestead exemption, classification or deferral has its own 30 day limit, counted from the day the denial letter went out. The board handles value and exemptions only. Tax rates are set at the budget hearings of the taxing authorities in September and October. Owners of a rental or an agricultural parcel can ask the appraiser's office, which has agricultural classification, mobile home and tangible property pages on its site, whether a separate filing applies.

Before you file, gather what supports your number: recent comparable sales, photos of condition problems, and repair estimates. Staff at the appraiser's office will often correct a plain error in square footage or exemption status without a hearing.

faqs.q: When does Hernando County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Payment is accepted through the end of March. After that the tax collector adds 3% interest to what is owed, along with advertising and collection fees.

faqs.q: What discount does Hernando County give for paying early?
faqs.a: The discount starts at 4 percent for November and drops a point each month through February. March has none, and the postmark sets the date for current-year payments.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Hernando County tax bill by card?
faqs.a: Yes, with a $2.75 minimum or 2.5% processing fee charged by a third-party vendor. E-checks are free online for current and delinquent bills, and tax deed payments need certified funds.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the Hernando County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Apply with the property appraiser at an office, by mail or on the online portal. The 2027 filing deadline is March 1, 2027, and the home must be your permanent residence on January 1.

faqs.q: Who runs the Hernando County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: The tax collector, online through LienHub at the end of May each year. Bidders register with LienHub, and parcels are offered one at a time in parcel number order.
